scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Rhythm of the Ancestors
This is Ukusina. Traditional.
on_screen: Title card: Ukusina · South Africa · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Ukusina originates from the coastal region of South Africa among the Zulu people.
It has been passed down primarily through oral traditions, with specific historical origins not well-documented.
It is currently preserved through cultural programs and festivals like the Zulu Reed Dance.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Ukusina is performed at weddings, memorial services, and coming-of-age ceremonies.
It serves as a way to communicate with ancestors and request their blessings and protection.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform powerful kicks in any direction and stamp their feet into the ground.
The dance is led by an induna who sets the pace.
Dancers move in line or circular formations while keeping time with the music.
Watch for Powerful kicks, Stamping.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is based on the rhythmic beat of traditional Zulu drums and other percussion instruments.
A song leader sings interlocking word phrases to guide the performance.
Listen for the Traditional Zulu drums, Other percussion instruments.
The music is driven by the rhythmic beat of traditional Zulu drums and percussion, accompanied by a song leader who uses interlocking vocal phrases.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear intricate beadwork, animal skin skirts (such as cow or goat), and feathers.
Men may wear an ibheshu or isikhakha, while women may wear an isidwaba.
Feathers are used in headpieces and armbands for spiritual significance.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Ukusina is considered a fundamental component of religious life, used to communicate with ancestor spirits; outsiders should observe with respect for its ritual function.
